question: How does the token audit get from my agent's API call to the report page?
subject: From API call to token report
answer: A small recorder sits between your agent and the AI, counts every token it really uses, and turns those counts into a ranked list of what wastes them.

scope.start: your agent sends a request to the model API

steps.title: Your agent asks the AI a question
steps.see: Nothing changes. Your agent works the way it always does.
steps.behind: Its messages go through a small recorder program on your computer instead of straight to the AI company.

steps.title: The recorder passes the message on, untouched
steps.see: Answers arrive as usual, just as fast.
steps.behind: It keeps nothing private. It only notes how big each part of the message is.

steps.title: The AI company reports what it used
steps.behind: Every answer comes with an exact count of tokens used. The recorder writes that count down, one line per question.

steps.title: Your agent gets its answer
steps.see: The same answer it would have got anyway.
steps.behind: If a spending limit is reached, the recorder refuses politely instead of passing the message on.

steps.title: After a few runs, a checker reads the notes
steps.see: Nothing. This happens after your agent has finished.
steps.behind: It adds everything up, finds where most tokens went, and flags 18 known kinds of waste.

steps.title: Claude checks each flag against your code
steps.see: Claude may ask to look at a few files.
steps.behind: Each flag is only a lead. Claude finds the exact line that causes it and works out how much it really costs.

steps.title: You get one clear page
steps.see: A page with three big numbers, a map of your agent, and every problem ranked by cost.
steps.behind: A builder program refuses to make the page until nothing is missing.

plain.analogy: Like a counter at a toll booth: cars drive through untouched, and at the end of the day you know exactly which lanes were busiest and why.
worth: The recorder never saves your messages or your key. It keeps only sizes and counts.
Once a spending limit is hit, it stops passing messages on, so a runaway agent can't run up a bill.
Each task runs at least three times, because AI answers vary from run to run.

terms.plain: a small piece of text, about four letters. AI companies count and charge by them.

summary: `usage_proxy.py` is a stdlib `ThreadingHTTPServer` that the agent reaches through `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. For each model call it records request block sizes and hashes, enforces a token budget, forwards the raw bytes with `Accept-Encoding: identity`, reads `usage` from the JSON body or the SSE events, and appends one JSONL record per call before replying. `analyze_trace.py` turns 3+ run files into stats, a by-source attribution, and detector findings; Claude confirms each finding in code and writes the audit JSON, which `build_report.py` validates and renders.

messages.note: Over budget? Record the call and answer 400 (no retry)

trace.how: HTTP POST `/v1/messages` (SDK base URL points at the proxy)
trace.data: the full Messages request body and headers, including `x-api-key`

trace.how: `urllib` request to the upstream URL, timeout 600 s
trace.data: the same body; headers minus `host`, `content-length`, `accept-encoding`, `connection`; adds `Accept-Encoding: identity`

trace.how: append one JSON line under a lock
trace.data: usage, block sizes, hashes, tool names, status, latency; no keys or content

trace.how: HTTP response, written after the record
trace.data: the upstream status, headers, and body bytes unchanged (streamed line by line for SSE)
JSONL records, one file per run
per-run stats, median run, attribution, findings with `tokens_involved`

trace.how: reads the agent's code for each finding (skill step 5)
trace.data: file:line evidence, real waste, fix, risk

trace.how: exit code and stdout or stderr
trace.data: `report.html`, or a list of missing fields

external.name: Anthropic Messages API
external.purpose: Runs the model the agent calls; its `usage` field is the only source of measured token counts.
external.auth: The agent's own `x-api-key` header, passed through untouched and never written to the trace.
external.sends: Everything the agent sends: prompts, tool results, any personal data in them. The proxy adds nothing.
external.limits: Upstream rate limits apply as usual; the proxy adds its own `--budget` cap (HTTP 400 when reached).
external.whenDown: The upstream error status and body pass through unchanged and are recorded with `usage: null`.

data.notes: Append-only; a lock serializes writes from concurrent requests.
Plain files; nothing is shared between audits.

timing: Steps 1–4 happen inside each model call; the proxy adds one local hop plus a file append.
The record is written before the reply (non-stream) or before the connection closes (stream), so the trace is complete when the agent continues.
Steps 5–9 run once, after all runs finish.
security: The API key passes through in memory only; tests assert it never reaches the trace file.
Message content is never written: only estimated sizes, SHA-1 prefixes, and tool names.
The proxy binds to `127.0.0.1` by default, so only local processes can use it.

config.name: --budget
config.effect: token cap; past it, calls get HTTP 400 so SDKs don't retry

config.name: --upstream
config.effect: where to forward; defaults per provider

config.name: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL / OPENAI_BASE_URL
config.effect: how the agent is pointed at the proxy without code changes

performance: Bodies are read fully into memory (non-stream); fine for API-sized payloads.
`Accept-Encoding: identity` disables compression upstream so usage can be parsed; slightly more bytes on the wire.

failures.userSees: The agent gets an HTTP 400 `budget_exceeded` error
failures.codeDoes: Records a `blocked: true` line, answers 400 without calling upstream

failures.userSees: The same error the API sent
failures.codeDoes: Passes status and body through; records `usage: null`

failures.userSees: No page; a list of missing fields

debug: Run the agent once through the proxy and read the trace: `tail -f audit/traces/<task>-run1.jsonl`.
Break in `do_POST` (`usage_proxy.py:295`) to see each request as it arrives.
Tests cover streaming, errors, budget, and key safety: `python3 -m unittest discover -s src/agents/auditing-agent-token-usage/tests`.
No API key? `tests/harness.py` runs any agent against the fake API through the real proxy.
open: Bedrock and Vertex sign each request, so the proxy can't sit in the path; the skill falls back to logging in code (`references/instrumenting.md`).
noticed: `do_GET` forwards requests but records nothing; fine today, since model calls are POSTs.
